results: 1. Comprehensive ocular motility examination with alternate-cover testing, prism measurements, and assessment of head-tilt response
nystagmus: direction and whether it changes with gaze: no nystagmus
adduction in horizontal gaze (each eye): limited adduction of the RIGHT eye that fails to cross the midline, with abducting nystagmus of the left eye on left gaze - mimics an INO
abducting nystagmus of the fellow eye: absent
skew deviation / alternating cover test: no vertical misalignment
ocular torsion and head tilt: none
2. Forced-duction testing of the affected eye
forced duction test: restriction consistent with a mechanical cause
3. Thin-slice CT of the orbits and facial bones without contrast
4. Complete ophthalmologic examination, including dilated fundus examination and formal visual fields
5. Orthoptic Hess-Lancaster or Lees screen examination
dx_raw:
DIAGNOSIS: Traumatic right medial orbital wall blowout fracture with entrapment of the right medial rectus muscle, causing restrictive adduction deficit that mimics internuclear ophthalmoplegia

Alternative 1: Traumatic right medial rectus muscle contusion, laceration, or post-traumatic scarring causing mechanical restriction

Alternative 2: Right orbital hematoma or soft-tissue impingement producing mechanical restriction

Alternative 3: Traumatic right oculomotor nerve palsy (less likely given the positive forced-duction test)
